name: Confluex
manufacturer: Novafold Pharmaceuticals (restricted medical formulation); Nightshade Pharmatech (recreational variant)
description: A bilateral neural-synchronization compound administered to two or more individuals simultaneously, creating a temporary shared sensory and proprioceptive bridge between compatible BCI systems. Originally developed for rehabilitation — allowing a patient to feel and use a prosthetic limb by synchronizing with a therapist's motor signals — Confluex has been widely adopted as a recreational intimacy drug and, covertly, as a tactical coordination tool. Both users experience each other's sensory input and, at higher doses, emotional states, creating a profound and often destabilizing sense of shared identity.
effects: Bidirectional sensory sharing between synchronized users
Shared proprioception — each user feels the other's body position and movement
Emotional state bleedthrough at doses above 0.4ml equivalent
Tactical users report near-telepathic combat coordination
Profound intimacy and dissolution of self/other boundary
Augments temporarily respond to either user's motor intent
side_effects: Identity diffusion — temporary confusion about which thoughts and sensations are your own
Desynchronization shock if the link is broken suddenly (nausea, vertigo, acute anxiety)
Emotional contamination — absorbing the other user's trauma, fear, or rage involuntarily
Rare: persistent echo syndrome where one user continues to feel phantom sensations from the other days after dosing
BCI compatibility conflicts causing sharp neural feedback pain
Psychological dependency on the sensation of shared identity
duration: 90 minutes to 3 hours depending on dose and BCI compatibility
cultural_context: Confluex occupies a strange social position — it's the drug people take when they want to be truly known by someone, or when they want to know someone completely. In Tier 3 and 4 relationship culture it's used as an intimacy ritual, sometimes at major life milestones, sometimes recreationally. In Tier 1 and 2 it has a harder edge: tactical crews use it for coordination, but also because the Shelf produces so much psychological isolation that the temporary obliteration of loneliness is worth the crash. Confessor cults use it as a sacrament. There are documented cases of two people Confluent during one partner's death — the survivor rarely emerges unchanged.
story_hooks: A grieving Tier 3 professional paid a gray-market clinic to Confluent them with a recently deceased partner using a recorded neural snapshot — the experience has left them unable to fully distinguish their own memories from the recording. They're deteriorating, and the clinic has disappeared.

A tactical crew used Confluex during a job and something went wrong during forced desynchronization — now all four members are sharing involuntary emotional bleedthrough days later, and one of them experienced something during the sync that the others are afraid to remember.

Nightshade Pharmatech's recreational Confluex variant has a hidden secondary effect: it creates a faint, persistent BCI signature link between users that a third party with the right hardware can exploit for surveillance. Someone has been farming intimate data from recreational users for months.
